sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF M.V.
ACT, PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 05.03.2018 IN MVC NO.1007/2014 PASSED BY THE COURT OF THE II ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT AT TUMAKURU AND ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION AWARD AMOUNT.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THROUGH PHYSICAL HEARING/VIDEO CONFERENCING THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 05.03.2018 passed in MVC No.1007/2014 by the Court of the II Additional Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Tumakuru (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Tumakuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.
Brief facts of the case are as follows:

On 31.07.2013 at about 4.45 p.m. the petitioner while proceeding to her house from school by walk, met with an accident near Maralur Dinne Main road, Tumakuru, at that time, a Hero Honda motor bike bearing registration No.KA-06-E-7772 being driven in a rash and negligent manner dashed against her.
The petitioner was a minor girl at the time of the accident.
The motor cycle was owned by respondent No.1.

Varalakshmi vs Sri. Syed Dasthagir on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53267230/
2 4.

The Tribunal based on the pleadings and evidence let-in, came to the conclusion that the insurance policy produced by the petitioner alleging that the offending motor cycle was duly insured with respondent No.2 is a fake insurance policy and has fastened the liability on respondent No.1 - owner and has awarded a compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner has preferred this appeal.
Respondent No.1 though served has remained absent and unrepresented.
6. The petitioner, in the accident has suffered fracture of both bones of left leg.

PW-2, the Doctor who has examined the petitioner, in his evidence has opined that petitioner has suffered 36%
disability to her left lower limb and 12% disability to the whole body.
His evidence in this regard has not been impeached.
7. The petitioner was aged about 9 years at the time of accident.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MASTER MALLIKARJUN VS. DIVISIONAL MANAGER, THE NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND ANOTHER - AIR 2014 SC 736, in respect of minors when the whole body disability is between 10% to 30%, it has been held that a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- is the appropriate compensation to be awarded towards pain and suffering, future mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience and discomfort and loss of amenities on account of permanent disability.

entities.text: MASTER MALLIKARJUN VS. DIVISIONAL MANAGER, THE NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND ANOTHER - AIR 2014 SC 736
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In my opinion, under the given facts and circumstances of the case, it is appropriate to award the same amount.

8. It is also submitted that the petitioner was an inpatient for a period of 15 days and given the nature of injuries, three months has to be considered as the recovery period, which would warrant at least one of the parent to take care of her and for that reason, a sum of Rs.24,000/- is hereby awarded towards 'loss of earning to the parents due to the injury to the petitioner'.
No evidence is let-in by the petitioner regarding medical expenses and hence, no amount can be awarded towards the same.

9. Thus, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.1,50,000/- to Rs.3,24,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the petition before the Tribunal till realization payable by respondent No.1 (owner of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-06-E-7772).
However, petitioner is not entitled for interest for a period of 196 days, the delay in NC: 2023:KHC:33479 filing the appeal.
Respondent No.1 shall pay the enhanced amount within a period of six weeks from today.
The appeal against respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.
10. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part.
Office to draw modified award accordingly.
11. Registry to return the records to the jurisdictional Tribunal forthwith.
